extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: MVBench is a comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark that covers 20 challenging video tasks requiring a broad spectrum of temporal skills, ranging from perception to cognition.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li; Yali Wang; Yinan He; Yizhuo Li; Yi Wang; Yi Liu; Zun Wang; Jilan Xu; Guo Chen; Ping Luo; Limin Wang; Yu Qiao
extraction.citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao. MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. arXiv:2311.17005v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by selecting videos and annotations from 11 existing public video benchmarks, which were then filtered based on temporal sensitivity and question difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations from 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We automatically convert the video annotations into this format via LLMs. Specifically, we first use ChatGPT to generate a question for each video, based on the task definition. Then, we create the corresponding answer options via Template-Based Construction or LLM-Based Generation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: comprehensively evaluating the temporal perception capabilities of MLLMs in the open world
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We automatically convert the video annotations into multiple-choice QA format via LLMs (ChatGPT), generating questions and converting open-ended QAs into multiple-choice QAs with answer options. For STAR, we enhance the challenge by randomly shifting the start or end points of the video clips. We randomly sample 3 to 5 answer options from the available candidates, shuffle the option order, and use LLM to guarantee that all the answer options of a question are of similar and reasonable lengths.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We eliminate short clips which generally contain negligible motions, and also delete extremely long videos, selecting videos with intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s. For CLEVRER, we exclude questions that necessitate more than 10 conditions for describing specific events.
